name: Gann's Reclamation
summary: In the southern Barrens, Gann's Reclamation turns toward Bael Modan. Gann Stonespire, a tauren exile, asks you to strike at the dig after it drove him from his clan's ancestral home and hunting grounds.

sections.title: A Displaced Tribe
sections.body: Gann Stonespire walks alone along the southern road, seeking justice for his fallen kin. His clan lived among the red bluffs south of the Barrens. Dwarves from Ironforge built Bael Modan there, driving the tauren out or killing them to make room for quarries and trenches. Gann says peaceful protests and diplomacy failed. Now he seeks vengeance for his displaced and slain clan.

sections.title: The Ruins of Bael Modan
sections.body: At Bael Modan, dwarven excavators tear into the hills with steam engines and explosives. Prospector Khazgorm leads the dig deep underground. Gann asks you to thin the ranks of Bael'dun excavators and foremen, kill Khazgorm, and bring back the prospector's personal excavation notes. He wants to learn what the Alliance expedition seeks in the sacred soil.

faq.answer: Gann Stonespire is a solitary tauren survivor whose tribe once lived in the southern Barrens. Dwarven excavators drove his people from their land and killed those who resisted. Now he walks the southern highway, seeking justice and revenge against the Alliance dig site.

faq.q: Why are the dwarves in the Barrens?
aliases: why are dwarves at bael modan
faq.answer: The dwarves belong to an Ironforge expedition called the Bael'dun. They built a keep and excavation at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens, where their blasting and noisy machines tear apart the hills despite the native tauren inhabitants.
Prospector Khazgorm leads the dwarven excavation south of the Bael Modan fortress. Gann blames him for the desecration of his ancestral grounds and demands his journal as proof of his death.

faq.q: Where can Gann Stonespire be found?
faq.answer: Gann Stonespire walks along the road in the far southern Barrens, west of the Bael Modan fortress and north of the road toward the Great Lift and Thousand Needles.

faq.q: Did Gann try to resolve this peacefully?
faq.answer: Yes. Gann says he tried diplomacy and other peaceful means to stop the destruction of his ancestral lands. The dwarves dismissed his efforts and kept blasting the hills, so he turned to violence.
After Gann receives Khazgorm's journal, he studies the notes to understand the dwarves' technology and plans. Then he seeks to sabotage their heavy machinery.

angles.text: As a Shu'halo, you can see Gann's plight as an infuriating reminder that the Alliance shows little respect for the Earth Mother. Dynamite and iron gears tear apart ancestral burial grounds.
As a member of the Horde, you see Bael Modan as a fortified Alliance stronghold deep in Kalimdor. Defending Gann's claim is an act of honor and a way to contain that stronghold.
As a shaman, you know Bael Modan's blasting and deep trenches wound the surrounding earth spirits. Gann's campaign is a necessary cleansing of that elemental disruption.
